ProgramName: Master of Science in Accountancy
Concentration: Taxation emphasis, Audit and fraud examination emphasis
Description: Designed for professionals who want to accelerate their accounting career, this program explores the evolving role of accounting in global business.  Students engage in case studies and practical research to build advanced expertise in areas like auditing, financial accounting, reporting, and taxes.  The program is customizable to align with career goals in various sectors, including auditing, tax compliance, nonprofit, or governmental accounting.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Adult, Organizational Learning and Leadership
Concentration: leading healthy organizations, human resource development, higher education leadership, organizational systems innovation and change
Description: This program is designed for professionals from a wide range of fields who want to strengthen their leadership skills, inspire learning, lead with impact, and facilitate meaningful organizational change. The online course delivery model addresses the practical needs of working professionals, allowing them to balance full-time work, family responsibilities, and education. Graduates are prepared for influential positions requiring organizational insight, strategic thinking, and team management.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Agricultural Education
Description: This program prepares students for careers in high school education or university extension, which are in high demand. Students gain skills to teach leadership and life skills to youth and adults through hands-on agricultural learning. The curriculum includes advanced teaching methods, communication, leadership, and research to build a strong foundation for leading educational programs.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Animal Science
Concentration: animal nutrition, reproductive physiology, meat science, animal breeding, muscle biology and growth
Description: A Master of Science in Animal Science prepares you to contribute to advancements in animal care, breeding, meat and dairy quality, and the sustainability of animal agriculture. The program will prepare you to develop specialized knowledge in areas such as animal nutrition, reproductive physiology, meat science, animal breeding, muscle biology and growth. You will also gain research experience by designing and completing a thesis project that addresses an important question in animal agriculture.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration
Concentration: General Management, J.D./M.B.A. concurrent program
Description: The University of Idaho's Master of Business Administration (MBA) is a fully online, 39-credit program designed to develop strategic, analytical, and leadership skills. The curriculum consists of 27 core credits and 12 elective credits, with courses delivered in 8-week sessions, allowing most students to complete the degree in 15–24 months.  The program is tailored for professionals seeking to advance their careers by providing practical business insights and leadership development.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemical Engineering
Description: In this program, you'll explore how chemical processes work and gain the skills needed for research or industrial careers. Students team up with experienced faculty members to study topics like reaction systems, paper production methods, nanotechnology, and ways to clean up hazardous materials. Hands-on experience is a key part of learning, utilizing cutting-edge lab equipment to explore real-world problems.
ScholarshipType: NASA Idaho Space Grant Consortium (ISGC)##National Science Foundation (NSF) Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemistry
Concentration: Analytical, Inorganic, Organic, Physical, Bio-organic chemistry, Biophysical chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Medicinal chemistry, Nanomaterials
Description: Prepare for a career in chemical research and development by focusing on a branch of chemistry that interests you, including analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry.  Using sophisticated instruments, you may work to develop new materials for medicine, agriculture, food production, or industry.  The program also offers opportunities for interdisciplinary research in areas like bio-organic chemistry, biophysical chemistry, environmental chemistry, medicinal chemistry, and nanomaterials.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Civil Engineering
Concentration: Environmental Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Hydraulics and Water Resources Engineering, Ecohydraulics, Structural Engineering, Transportation Engineering, Highway and Pavement Materials
Description: The Master of Science in Civil Engineering program at the University of Idaho provides advanced education in designing and managing essential infrastructure like highways, bridges, and water systems. A thesis is required, and the program combines courses in geological engineering, geology, civil engineering, and hydrogeology to prepare students for complex infrastructure projects and the evaluation of geologic hazards.
ProgramCategory: Civil Engineering##Environmental Engineering##Structural Engineering##Traffic & Transportation Engineering##Water Resource Management

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computational Biology
Concentration: Thesis Track, Non-Thesis Track
Description: The Master of Science in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology at the University of Idaho provides interdisciplinary training that integrates biology, mathematics, statistics, and computer science. The program is designed to prepare students to analyze complex biological data and contribute to research in fields like genetics, genomics, and mathematical modeling. Students will complete 30 credits of coursework, including core classes and advanced courses tailored to their research interests.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Engineering
Concentration: Digital hardware design, digital systems design, computer systems
Description: The Master of Science in Computer Engineering at the University of Idaho blends computer science and electrical engineering to prepare students for careers in digital systems and hardware design. The program focuses on the complex relationship between hardware and software, emphasizing digital computer architecture, programming, and practical applications. A thesis is a required component of this degree.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science
Concentration: digital hardware design, digital systems design, computer systems
Description: A graduate degree in computer science from the University of Idaho prepares students for a lifetime of discovery, enabling them to advance the state of the art in computing. The program develops critical thinking, investigatory, and expository skills, teaching the foundations of computer science theory and application. Students learn to understand important issues, resolve open problems, and present solutions effectively.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Creative Writing
Concentration: Fiction, Poetry, Nonfiction
Description: The Master of Fine Arts in Creative Writing is a three-year, fully funded program designed as the terminal degree for individuals aspiring to teach creative writing at the university level. The curriculum offers intensive theoretical and practical training in fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction, culminating in a book-length creative thesis.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Crop Science
Concentration: thesis, non-thesis
Description: This program prepares students for the in-depth study of the production, protection, breeding, and genetics of plants. Students gain a sophisticated understanding of this interdisciplinary field with specialized skills in areas like biotechnology, weed science, crop management, and plant pathology. Research is conducted alongside faculty experts in on-campus plant science farms, climate-controlled greenhouses, and laboratories.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Curriculum and Instruction
Concentration: English as a Second Language (ESL), Curriculum Development, Coaching and Mentorship
Description: Designed for licensed teachers, the Master of Education (M.Ed.) in Curriculum and Instruction helps educators become more confident, creative, and innovative leaders.  The program focuses on strengthening abilities in designing instruction, assessing student learning, and adapting to diverse student needs through a flexible, non-thesis path.  Students explore effective curriculum strategies, support for diverse learners, and the use of research to improve instruction.
ProgramCategory: Education##Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Drama
Concentration: Performance, Dramatic Writing, Directing, Design/Technology (scenery, costumes or lighting)
Description: The Master of Fine Arts in Drama at the University of Idaho is a rigorous, three-year program designed for talented students preparing for a career in professional theatre.  The program offers tracks in performance, dramatic writing, directing, and design/technology, providing intensive training and hands-on opportunities in live productions.  It is the only MFA in Theatre in Idaho and is known for producing skilled and accomplished theatre professionals.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Education
Concentration: English as a Second Language (ESL)
Description: The Master of Arts in Education at the University of Idaho offers advanced professional courses designed to build a strong foundation in teacher education. It is tailored for individuals who already hold a bachelor's degree in the subject they wish to teach, allowing them to pursue this program to gain essential teaching strategies and learning theories. The curriculum prepares graduates to meet the needs of their future students and thrive in a teaching career.
ProgramCategory: Education##Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages

ProgramName: Master of Science in Educational Administration
Concentration: Special Education (SE) director
Description: The Master of Science in Educational Administration prepares students for leadership roles in elementary or secondary school administration, with a focus on practical leadership skills, instructional leadership, and managing curriculum. The program incorporates components of schools as learning organizations to support continuous improvement in student achievement, faculty development, and community engagement. Coursework covers topics such as educational policy, school finance, and legal and ethical principles in education.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Educational Leadership
Description: The Master of Education in Educational Leadership at the University of Idaho prepares educators for leadership roles such as principal or program administrator. The program focuses on providing the knowledge and tools to shape policy, guide institutional improvement, and enhance student outcomes. It is CAEP certified and aligned with state certification requirements for administrative licensure, offering a direct path to leadership positions.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering
Concentration: Power and energy systems, Electromagnetic wave propagation, Microelectronics, Electronic packaging
Description: The Master of Science in Electrical Engineering at the University of Idaho offers advanced training and hands-on research in areas like power and energy systems, electronics, and microelectronics. As a student in this nationally-recognized program, you will explore the principles behind electrical systems and gain advanced skills to design innovative solutions. The program provides opportunities to work alongside expert faculty on research that addresses current industry challenges.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in English
Concentration: Literature, Teaching, Creative Writing, Rhetoric and Composition
Description: Advanced literary studies challenge you to think and write critically about how words can reflect and shape the world.  Designed to prepare students for doctoral studies or teaching careers, the program allows you to tailor your studies to fit your career goals in teaching, writing, or editing.  Students explore language, literature, composition, rhetoric, and literary theory through independent scholarly research.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Entomology
Concentration: Thesis, Non-Thesis
Description: This program is the only graduate program in entomology in the state of Idaho, providing students with a deep understanding of insects and their effects on agriculture, human health, and the environment.  As a graduate student, you will delve into advanced subjects such as insect systems, biodiversity, ecology, physiology, and pest management.  The program offers both thesis and non-thesis options.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Environmental Science
Concentration: Thesis, Non-thesis
Description: The Master of Science in Environmental Science at the University of Idaho is an interdisciplinary program designed for those committed to protecting and conserving the environment.  It explores the impact of natural and human-made processes on the planet's physical systems, covering key areas like waste management, environmental pollution, policy, water science, and land use.  The program offers both a campus-based thesis option for research-focused careers and a flexible non-thesis option that can be completed online or on campus for working professionals.
ProgramCategory: Environmental Science##Water Resource Management##Ecology##Environmental Studies##Environmental Management

ProgramName: Master of Science in Experimental Psychology
Concentration: thesis, non-thesis
Description: The Master of Science in Psychology program at the University of Idaho focuses on the intersection of psychology, engineering, and user experience, preparing students for roles in technology and product design. This research-driven program explores how users process information, make decisions, and interact with digital and physical systems. The curriculum is designed to shape the design of products, workspaces, and environments to enhance performance, usability, and well-being.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Fire Ecology
Concentration: Fire Ecology and Management
Description: The Master of Natural Resources (MNR) with a Fire Ecology and Management option is an interdisciplinary, course-based graduate program designed for professionals seeking to advance their careers.  It provides a science-based approach to managing wildland fire by integrating perspectives from ecology, planning, policy, society, and technology.  The program aims to deepen understanding of fire science, fuels management, ecological restoration, and fire-related policy to address contemporary wildfire challenges.
ProgramCategory: Ecology##Forestry##Environmental Science##Environmental Management##Natural Science##Wildlife Management##Water Resource Management

ProgramName: Master of Science in Fire Management
Concentration: Fire Ecology and Management
Description: The Master of Natural Resources (MNR) with a Fire Ecology and Management option is an interdisciplinary, course-based graduate program designed for professionals seeking to advance their careers. It provides a science-based approach to managing wildland fire by integrating key perspectives from ecology, planning, policy, and technology. The program is flexible, can be completed fully online, and is open to students from all academic backgrounds.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Food Science
Concentration: Thesis, non-thesis
Description: The Master of Science in food science program is designed to provide advanced training for students seeking careers in the food industry, government or regulatory agencies.  The program emphasizes coursework in food chemistry, food engineering, food microbiology, sensory science, and safety, along with a thesis or applied project.  Research at this level generally focuses on solving practical problems related to food quality, safety, or product development.
ProgramCategory: Food Science##Culinary/Food Studies##Agriculture Plant Sciences##Agriculture Animal Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Science in Geography
Concentration: Cultural & Political Ecology, Geospatial Science, Fluvial Geomorphology, Biogeography
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Geography at the University of Idaho prepares students to address complex geographical and environmental issues by providing advanced training in physical, human, and technical geography.  The program emphasizes fieldwork, laboratory analysis, GIS, spatial statistics, and other contemporary scientific methods.  It equips students with critical thinking skills, problem-solving abilities, and knowledge in geographic theory for professional and academic careers.
ProgramCategory: Geography##Geographic Information Systems##Remote Sensing & Geospatial Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Science in Geological Engineering
Concentration: Thesis, Non-thesis
Description: This joint program between the College of Engineering and College of Science provides integrated training in engineering design, geoscience fundamentals, and applied environmental problem-solving. Students take courses in geological and civil engineering, hydrogeology, and site characterization, preparing them to assist in the design and construction of civil engineering projects, evaluate geologic hazards, and develop natural energy resources. The degree is available with either a thesis or non-thesis option.
ScholarshipType: Funding options are available through the College of Graduate Studies.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Geology
Concentration: geochemistry, geomorphology, paleontology, petrology, sedimentology, stratigraphy
Description: The M.S. in Geology program at the University of Idaho provides students with advanced training in both geological theory and modern field observation strategies. It offers opportunities for in-depth research in areas like geochemistry, geomorphology, and paleontology, preparing students for careers in industry, academia, or government. The program emphasizes solving environmental problems and understanding challenges such as erosion and climate change.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Merit-based, Need-based

ProgramName: Master of Arts in History
Concentration: U.S. History I (early), U.S. History II (modern), Ancient Mediterranean, Medieval Europe, Modern Europe, Latin America, Modern Asia, gender and sexuality, visual and material culture, environmental history, intellectual and cultural history, public history, empire and colonialism, film history, race and ethnicity
Description: In this program, you will deepen your understanding of the human experience through advanced study and research spanning centuries, continents and cultures.  The work toward an M.A. degree stresses preparation for research as well as a balanced course program.  Students will contextualize, evaluate, and interpret primary source materials within broad scholarly debate to create a meaningful contribution to historical scholarship.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Hydrology
Concentration: Thesis Option, Non-thesis Professional Option
Description: The Master of Science in Groundwater Hydrology prepares working professionals in geology, geological engineering, environmental science, and water use planning with practical concepts and real-world analytical skills. Students gain proficiency in analyzing and interpreting hydrological data, and designing and computing data from groundwater tests. Graduates are prepared to lead water management projects, develop sustainable practices, and inform policy related to water use.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Industrial Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Industrial Engineering (MSIE) is designed for students seeking an advanced, research-focused degree for careers in industry, government, or engineering sciences, or as preparation for a Ph.D. program.  The program is intended for full-time, on-campus students and requires the completion of a thesis.  A total of 30 credits is required for the degree.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Integrated Architecture and Design
Concentration: Virtual Technology and Design, Architecture, Interior Architecture & Design, Environmental Design / Landscape Architecture, Art & Design
Description: The Master of Science in Integrated Architecture and Design at the University of Idaho is a research-driven, interdisciplinary program that challenges students to think beyond traditional design. It explores the connections between architecture, virtual technology and design, landscape architecture, interior architecture and design, and art to develop forward-thinking solutions. The program is recognized as a STEM-designated degree.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies
Description: The Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies at the University of Idaho allows students to design a customized program of study by integrating coursework from two or more academic departments. This flexible degree is tailored to meet unique academic and professional goals, offering both thesis and non-thesis options. Students work with a faculty mentor to create their curriculum and conduct independent research.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Kinesiology
Concentration: Exercise, sport and health sciences, Sport and recreation management, Physical activity and dance pedagogy
Description: The Master of Science in Kinesiology at the University of Idaho focuses on the advanced study of human movement, exercise, sport performance, health, and wellness. The program provides hands-on learning and opportunities for students to conduct research in various laboratory or field-based settings. It is designed to develop advanced knowledge and skills across a range of kinesiology and exercise science fields.

ProgramName: Master of Landscape Architecture
Concentration: Post-professional Pathway, First-professional Pathway, Green Infrastructure, Cultural Landscapes, Sustainability, Urban Design
Description: The Master of Landscape Architecture (M.L.A.) at the University of Idaho is an accredited professional degree that prepares students to address significant environmental challenges such as water conservation, green infrastructure, and urban resilience. The program offers two pathways: a shorter post-professional track for those with related undergraduate degrees, and a longer first-professional track for those with degrees in other fields. Students gain hands-on experience with technologies like 3D modeling and GIS, and can choose to study at the Moscow campus or the Boise Urban Design Center.

ProgramName: Master of Laws
Concentration: Democracy, Justice, and the American Legal System, Natural Resources and Environmental Law, Business Law and Entrepreneurship, Litigation and Alternative Dispute Resolution
Description: The Master of Laws (LL.M.) at the University of Idaho is a 24-credit program designed for completion within a nine-month timeframe. The curriculum begins with an introductory course to American Law and Legal Education, after which students can tailor their studies around specific interests within the college's areas of strength.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Materials Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering provides students with a strong foundation in materials science, including both theoretical study and hands-on experiments.  The program involves research in areas like nanotechnology, microelectronics, alternative energy applications, and advanced materials processing to solve real-world industry problems.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mathematics
Concentration: Thesis, Non-thesis, Bioinformatics and mathematical biology, Algebra, algebraic geometry and number theory, Analysis and differential equations, Combinatorics, Discrete geometry, Mathematics education, Probability and stochastic processes
Description: The Master of Science in Mathematics at the University of Idaho equips students with advanced mathematical principles to solve complex problems in various sectors like industry, economy, government, and science. The program offers opportunities for research and hands-on experience, focusing on areas such as bioinformatics, combinatorics, differential equations, algebra, and mathematics education. It is designed for individuals who wish to pursue careers in research and development, business and finance, or teaching.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Concentration: Thesis
Description: The Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering at the University of Idaho expands technical expertise through advanced coursework and hands-on research guided by expert faculty. This program helps students build analytical, experimental, and problem-solving skills to address complex real-world challenges. Students complete original research and a written thesis with a formal defense, preparing them for leadership roles in industry, research, or academia.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Molecular Biology
Concentration: Biology, Microbiology, Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
Description: In the Master of Science in Biology program at the University of Idaho, students can choose between two degree options: biology or microbiology, molecular biology and biochemistry.  Students work with faculty on research in areas like reproductive biology, evolution and ecology, neurobiology, or cellular and molecular biology, and gain experience in experimental design and teaching.

ProgramName: Master of Music
Concentration: music education, performance (with degree patterns in brass, choral conducting, keyboard, percussion, strings, voice and woodwinds), composition, piano pedagogy and performance studies, collaborative piano
Description: The Master of Music program is designed for professional performers, composers, and music educators in schools or studios. It serves as a terminal professional degree or as a foundation for doctoral studies, offering personalized instruction from accomplished faculty.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Natural Resources
Concentration: forest resources and conservation sciences, fire science, wildlife and fisheries resources, rangeland management, forest products
Description: The Master of Science in Natural Resources program at the University of Idaho is a research-based program that encompasses a wide range of natural resource disciplines and issues.  Students work with faculty on research exploring topics like landscapes after wildland fire, invasive species, remote sensing and GIS tools, wildlife habitats, and human interactions with the environment.  The program is designed for those who want to make an impact in natural resources management and enjoy conducting research.
ProgramCategory: Natural Science##Environmental Science##Forestry##Wildlife Management##Rangeland Resource Science##Water Resource Management##Remote Sensing & Geospatial Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Science in Natural Resources Conservation
Concentration: Forest Resources and Conservation Sciences, Fire Science, Wildlife and Fisheries Resources, Rangeland Management, Forest Products
Description: The Master of Science in Natural Resources encompasses a wide range of disciplines, including forest resources, conservation sciences, fire science, wildlife and fisheries resources, rangeland management, and forest products. Students work alongside internationally recognized faculty to lead independent research on a topic that supports their career goals in solving complex environmental challenges.
ProgramCategory: Natural Science##Environmental Science##Environmental Studies##Forestry##Wildlife Management##Water Resource Management##Ecology##Conservation##Rangeland Resource Science##Fisheries Biology

ProgramName: Master of Science in Natural Resources Management
Concentration: thesis, non-thesis
Description: The Master of Science in Natural Resources at the University of Idaho is a research-based program that encompasses a wide range of natural resource disciplines and issues. Students can choose a thesis or non-thesis track and will conduct independent research on a topic of interest to support their career goals.
ProgramCategory: Natural Science##Environmental Science##Environmental Studies##Forestry##Wildlife Management##Water Resource Management##Rangeland Resource Science##Fisheries Biology

ProgramName: Master of Science in Neuroscience
Concentration: neurobiology, cognitive neuroscience, computational neuroscience
Description: Merging biological, cognitive and computational neurosciences, this interdisciplinary program provides the broad academic foundation and diverse research experiences you need to study and contribute to the scientific understanding of brain and spinal cord function.  The program addresses all aspects of the highly integrated field to understand and model neurological function, including nervous system biology, cognitive and behavioral processes, and the applications of mathematics and computer science.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Nuclear Engineering
Concentration: Nuclear fuel processing and materials, Radioactive waste treatment and management, Thermal behavior and measurement, Nuclear systems design and modeling, Applications of nuclear process heat
Description: This program explores innovative, emissions-free nuclear power applications in electricity and hydrogen production, industry, medicine and national security. It is designed to meet the critical need for skilled nuclear engineers by offering advanced technical training and hands-on research experience. Graduates are prepared for careers in industry and government as radiological engineers, nuclear engineers, or nuclear process engineers.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Physics
Concentration: condensed matter physics, theoretical nuclear physics, astronomy and planetary science, biological physics
Description: In the Master of Science in Physics program at the University of Idaho, students explore the laws of the universe and gain research experience to prepare for contributions to the field.  Graduate students have opportunities to work with faculty on research in areas like condensed matter physics, theoretical nuclear physics, astronomy, planetary science, and biological physics.  The program is designed for those who want a physics-related career in applied research, development, computer science, engineering, or teaching.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Assistantships, Fellowships, Tuition Waivers

ProgramName: Master of Science in Plant Science
Concentration: Biotechnology, Weed Science, Crop Management, Plant Pathology, Thesis, Non-thesis
Description: The M.S. in Plant Science program at the University of Idaho provides an in-depth study of plant production, protection, breeding, and genetics. The program emphasizes hands-on experience through research in on-campus farms, climate-controlled greenhouses, and laboratories alongside faculty experts. It is designed to prepare students for leadership roles in agriculture, academia, government, and other industry sectors with a focus on interdisciplinary skills.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Political Science
Description: The Master of Arts in Political Science at the University of Idaho focuses on the study of political structures, processes, and public administration and policies.  Students in this program examine complex political relationships and learn to apply advanced concepts to real-world issues, developing strong research and analytical skills.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Psychology
Concentration: Human Factors
Description: The Master of Science in Psychology at the University of Idaho is a research-driven program that blends psychology, engineering, and user experience to prepare students for roles in tech and product design. Students explore how users process information and interact with systems, shaping the design of products and environments to enhance performance and usability. The program is offered both on-campus and online.

ProgramName: Master of Public Administration
Description: The Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.) at the University of Idaho is designed for students interested in leadership and management careers within local governments, communities, and non-profit organizations.  The program, offered both on-campus and online, focuses on improving practical and analytical skills to prepare students for public service.  It is a non-thesis program that requires an internship for students without prior public sector experience or field-based research for those with experience.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Sociology
Master of Science in Soil and Land Resources
Concentration: Thesis Option, Non-thesis Option
Description: This program provides expertise on the soil ecosystem and develops research skills to address soil-related issues for sustainable agriculture and the environment.  Much of the learning comes from independent research through a thesis, with opportunities for lab research on topics like heavy-metal contamination or fieldwork on water flow and sustainable crop production.  The program is designed for students with a science-related undergraduate degree who are interested in conducting independent research.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Soil Science
Concentration: thesis, non-thesis
Description: This program provides expertise on the soil ecosystem and develops research skills to address soil-related issues for sustainable agriculture and the environment. Much of the learning comes from independent research through a thesis, with opportunities to conduct lab research on topics like heavy-metal contamination or fieldwork on water flow and sustainable crop production.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Special Education
Concentration: Master's Degree with Certification in Special Education, Master's Degree for certified teachers, 4+1 program for B.S.Ed students
Description: This program is designed for both current educators and aspiring professionals who want to support students with mild to moderate disabilities, including learning disabilities, behavior challenges, and autism spectrum disorder. Students learn to design individualized curricula, support students' social and academic development, and help them build skills for life beyond the classroom. The program is offered through the College of Education, Health and Human Sciences.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Statistical Science
Description: The Master of Science in Statistical Science at the University of Idaho combines advanced mathematics and applied statistics with modern quantitative and computational techniques. Students learn to design and analyze experiments, plan and interpret surveys, and use numerical data to solve real-world problems. The program prepares graduates for analytical careers in a wide range of industries by developing skills in data management and analysis using tools like SAS and R.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Statistics
Concentration: Biostatistics, Statistical Computing, Data Science
Description: The Master of Science in Statistical Science at the University of Idaho is a program designed for those with an interest in analytical careers, combining advanced mathematics and applied statistics with modern quantitative and computational methods.  The curriculum prepares students to design and analyze experiments, interpret surveys, and use data to solve real-world problems in a variety of fields.  The program requires 30 credit hours and culminates in a capstone project involving a real-world data analysis problem.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Studio Art
Concentration: painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, graphic design, printmaking, interface design
Description: The Master of Fine Arts in art program at the University of Idaho is designed for aspiring professional studio artists and those who want to pursue a career in academia. The program emphasizes an integrated approach to art making and design, allowing students to work across disciplines to develop their creative versatility. This terminal degree culminates in a thesis that includes a solo exhibition of professional quality work and a written explanation of the creative process.
ProgramCategory: Art##Fine Arts##Studio Arts##Visual and Performing Arts##Graphic Design

ProgramName: Master of Science in Systems Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Industrial and Systems Engineering at the University of Idaho requires the completion of a thesis. Students will form a thesis committee, produce a written thesis, and undergo an oral defense and a closed session examination. A total of 30 credits is required for the degree.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Teaching
Concentration: Secondary Education, Mathematics
Description: The Master of Arts in Teaching (M.A.T.) for secondary education is designed for individuals who hold a bachelor's degree in the subject they wish to teach.  This one-year program equips students with advanced teaching strategies and learning theories to facilitate student success, leading to teacher certification for grades 6-12 in Idaho.
ProgramCategory: Education##Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages

ProgramName: Master of Science in Technology Management
Concentration: Industrial Project Management, Process Improvement, Innovation Industrial and Environmental Safety, Nuclear Technology Management
Description: The Master of Science in Technology Management prepares industry technical professionals for leadership roles in business, industry, or government. The program focuses on practical strategies and concepts in business, project management, process improvement, and leadership of technical teams. Students can tailor their studies to align with their interests and career goals.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre Arts
Concentration: design, directing, performance, technical production
Description: The Master of Fine Arts in Theatre Arts at the University of Idaho is a rigorous, three-year program designed for students seeking a career in professional theatre. The program offers tracks in design, directing, performance, and technical production, with curriculum tailored to the individual student. Progress is monitored through semesterly portfolio reviews or performance juries, culminating in a creative project and a comprehensive exam.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre Production
Concentration: design, directing, performance, technical production, dramatic writing, design/technology (scenery, costumes, or lighting)
Description: The Master of Fine Arts in Theatre Arts at the University of Idaho is a three-year, 60-credit hour program for students aiming for a career in professional theatre.  The program offers tracks in design, directing, performance, and technical production, with progress monitored through semesterly portfolio reviews or performance juries.  It is known for producing skilled theatre professionals and offers both on-campus and distance-based options to accommodate early-career and working professionals.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Veterinary Science
Concentration: animal nutrition, reproductive physiology, meats, animal breeding, muscle biology and growth
Description: The Master of Science in Animal and Veterinary Science at the University of Idaho is designed for students who wish to deepen their knowledge in the field. The program offers specializations and requires students to complete a thesis involving a research plan, data collection, and analysis. This is a cooperative program with Washington State University, providing access to facilities and faculty at both institutions.
ProgramCategory: Agriculture Animal Sciences##Veterinary Medicine##Animal Science##Biological Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Science in Water Resources
Concentration: Engineering and science, Science and management, Law, management and policy
Description: This interdisciplinary master's program blends coursework in hydrology, environmental science, resource management and policy, preparing students to manage water systems that support both people and ecosystems.  Students learn to collaborate with peers in other fields to define, research, and achieve creative and sustainable solutions to contemporary water problems.  Graduates are prepared for careers in water management agencies, environmental consulting firms, and governmental organizations focused on water sustainability.
ProgramCategory: Water Resource Management##Environmental Science##Environmental Management##Environmental Engineering

ProgramName: Master of Science in Zoology
Concentration: Thesis, Biology, Microbiology, Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
Description: In the Master of Science in Biology program, students work alongside faculty members who are leading research in reproductive biology, evolution and ecology, neurobiology, or cellular and molecular biology. Students design and conduct experiments, teach undergraduate students in the classroom and lab, and complete courses in professional development and ethical issues in biological research.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Accounting
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Accounting program at the University of Idaho provides students with the skills to analyze and manage complex financial information for various organizations.  The curriculum emphasizes hands-on learning and prepares students to become strategic business partners by covering areas like financial accounting, auditing, taxation, and reporting.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Economics
Concentration: Agribusiness, Applied Economics
Description: Professionals in this field apply their knowledge of economics, agriculture and business to help leaders in industry and government make important decisions about food production, rural development, and natural resources. Students explore the production, distribution and consumption of food and agricultural goods and services, developing strong problem-solving and analytical skills. Learning experiences include real-world projects, internships, and field trips.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Education
Concentration: Agricultural Economics, Animal Science, Plant Science, Horticulture
Description: This program prepares students to teach agriculture to grades 6-12 in both traditional classroom settings and informal educational environments.  Students develop a strong foundation in agricultural science while also learning curriculum design, classroom management, and how to advise student leadership organizations like FFA.  The curriculum includes hands-on learning through connections with national agricultural programs, hosting FFA events, and professional development activities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Animal and Veterinary Science
Concentration: Science/Pre-Veterinary, Production, Business, Dairy Science
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Animal and Veterinary Science is designed to prepare students for a future in veterinary health, fulfilling the undergraduate academic requirements for admission into a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (D.V.M.) program.  Students immerse themselves in the study of animal sciences, including reproduction, nutrition, growth, and health, gaining hands-on experience in on-campus labs and animal centers.  The curriculum integrates classroom learning with experiential opportunities to produce well-rounded professionals who can contribute to animal health and welfare.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Description: As an anthropology major at the University of Idaho, you will examine the world's diversity, explore human evolution, learn about societies of the past and present, and study the differences in languages, lifestyles, and physical attributes.  The program offers hands-on learning opportunities at the university's Alfred W. Bowers Laboratory of Anthropology and the Asian American Comparative Collection.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Anthropology
Description: As an anthropology major at the University of Idaho, you will explore global cultures, investigate human origins, and study how societies change over time. The program allows you to delve into topics like language, tradition, and material culture to better understand humanity. You will gain hands-on experience in the university's laboratories, working with artifacts and conducting archival research.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Architecture
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Architecture (B.S.Arch.) at the University of Idaho prepares students to design inspiring, meaningful, and long-lasting buildings and places. The curriculum focuses on applying the basic principles and practices of design, informed by history and theory, and provides exposure to architectural technologies through coursework and hands-on studio experiences. This four-year, pre-professional program qualifies students for entry-level architectural work and prepares them for a seamless transition into the professional Master of Architecture (M.Arch.) degree program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art
Concentration: graphic design, interactive design, painting, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Art program provides students with a comprehensive liberal arts education with an emphasis on art and design.  The curriculum integrates intensive studio instruction to develop technical skills, alongside courses in humanities, languages, and art history and theory.  This approach helps students become strong visual thinkers who understand the historical, cultural, and stylistic contexts of art.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art
Concentration: Graphic Design, Interaction Design, Painting, Sculpture, Printmaking, Photography/Digital Imaging, Ceramics, Drawing
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts (B.F.A.) in Studio Art and Design at the University of Idaho is a professional degree program for aspiring artists and designers. The curriculum focuses on strengthening creative voice, refining technical abilities, and developing versatile skills through hands-on studio courses and real-world projects. The program culminates in the development of a professional entry-level portfolio and an exhibition.

Students receive intensive studio instruction to develop technical skills in areas such as graphic design, painting, sculpture, printmaking, or ceramics.  The curriculum is designed to develop skills in visual thinking, critical analysis, and understanding the historical and cultural contexts of the visual arts.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological Engineering
Concentration: biomedical engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Biological Engineering at the University of Idaho integrates engineering principles with biology and chemistry to address challenges in human health, agriculture, and the environment.  This interdisciplinary program prepares students to develop solutions in areas like biotechnology, food systems, and clean energy, with coursework covering topics such as transport processes, bio-based products, and biomedical engineering.  The program also offers a pre-med track and an academic certificate in biomedical engineering, providing a strong foundation for careers in healthcare and other related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Broadcasting and Digital Media
Description: In the Bachelor of Arts in Broadcasting and Digital Media program, students learn to write, shoot video, edit, produce, and direct various types of broadcasts and digital formats.  The curriculum is designed to develop both the technical skills and broad media knowledge necessary to create and deliver content for news, sports, documentaries, marketing, and entertainment.  Students gain practical experience through hands-on opportunities like student productions, special projects, and university broadcast programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Broadcasting and Digital Media
Description: In the Bachelor of Science in Broadcasting and Digital Media program, students learn to write, shoot video, edit, produce, and direct various broadcast and digital formats.  The curriculum develops both the technical skills and broad media knowledge necessary to create and deliver content for news, sports, documentaries, marketing, and entertainment.  Students gain practical, hands-on experience through campus productions, video projects, and live broadcast opportunities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Economics
Concentration: General, Financial economics
Description: This program explores how the choices made by consumers, businesses, and governments regarding resources like time and money shape the economy and impact the business world. Students study essential economic concepts such as supply and demand, inflation, international trade, and government policy. The curriculum is designed to sharpen critical thinking, analysis, and research skills while building a strong foundation in marketing, finance, and management.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Concentration: Chemical Engineering Technical Elective, Biological Engineering Technical Elective, Material Science Engineering Technical Elective
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering program at the University of Idaho prepares students to design, optimize, and scale processes that transform raw materials into valuable products, ensuring safety and sustainability. Students develop strong foundations in science and engineering to create innovative solutions in sectors like energy, pharmaceuticals, and manufacturing. The program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
Concentration: environmental engineering, structural engineering, transportation engineering, hydraulics and ecohydraulics, hydrology and water resource engineering, geotechnical engineering, pavements and construction and materials engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering program at the University of Idaho teaches students to design and evaluate a wide range of civil engineering systems and processes. The curriculum focuses on applying technical skills to areas like sustainable water management, resilient transportation networks, and advanced materials to develop solutions for societal infrastructure. The field encompasses various sub-disciplines, including environmental, structural, transportation, geotechnical, and water resources engineering, all aimed at creating safe and resilient communities.
ProgramCategory: Civil Engineering##Engineering##Environmental Engineering##Structural Engineering##Traffic & Transportation Engineering##Water Resource Management

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering at the University of Idaho combines principles from electrical engineering and computer science to prepare students for careers in designing and testing new computer technologies. The curriculum covers both the software side of computing and the design of hardware like computer chips, circuit boards, and control systems. Students learn to apply their knowledge to develop technology for instrumentation, control, communication, and power-conversion systems.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
Concentration: algorithms and data, computer networking, cybersecurity, computer graphics, gaming and virtual environments, bioinformatics, software engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science program teaches students to design, develop, and test computing systems for various applications like business, communication, and healthcare. Students become proficient in multiple operating systems, programming languages, and computer architecture, with opportunities to apply their skills in real-world projects. The program is recognized as a STEM program by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Criminology
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Criminology at the University of Idaho provides a comprehensive understanding of criminal behavior, the societal response to crime, and the intricacies of the criminal justice system. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including homicide, policing, juvenile delinquency, and terrorism, preparing students for careers in law enforcement, corrections, victim advocacy, and research. The program emphasizes strong analytical, statistical, and research skills, with opportunities for real-world experience through internships.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Go Idaho! program, Western Undergraduate Exchange (WUE), Invitation to Idaho

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Criminology
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Criminology at the University of Idaho prepares students for careers in criminal justice, advocacy, courts, research, and investigation by taking a comprehensive look at the causes of crime and society's response to it.  The program helps students build strong analytical, statistical, and research skills while understanding criminal behaviors and the historical factors of the American criminal justice system.  It explores subjects like homicide, policing, juvenile delinquency, psychopathy, violent crime, terrorism, and white-collar crime.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Invitation to Idaho, Go Idaho!, Western Undergraduate Exchange (WUE)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Curriculum and Instruction
Concentration: Elementary Education, Secondary Education, Career and Technical Education
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Education (B.S.Ed.) with a major in Curriculum and Instruction provides the knowledge, skills, and experiences for teachers to work effectively with K-12 students and schools. The program emphasizes teacher education, preparing you to enhance your effectiveness as an educator through current research, contemporary instructional technologies, and the latest student-learning theories. Students benefit from collaborative relationships and extensive field experiences with partner schools.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Ecology and Conservation Biology
Description: This program provides a strong foundation in traditional sciences like biology and ecology, while also exploring social sciences to foster a deep, multidisciplinary understanding of the environmental, social, and political challenges threatening plants, animals, and ecosystems.  The curriculum is research-driven, culminating in a guided, hands-on senior thesis experience.  The goal is to promote biodiversity conservation through a science-based evaluation of ecological processes and human roles within ecosystems.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
Concentration: communications, integrated circuit design, power
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering at the University of Idaho teaches students to design and test electrical circuits and systems for a wide range of applications, including electronic devices, computers, and power systems. Students have opportunities to work on projects with organizations like the U.S. Navy and NASA. The program spans subdisciplines such as analog electronics, electric power, electromagnetics, computers, and communication and control systems.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Special Interest, Cultural and Diversity

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English
Concentration: Literature, Creative Writing, Professional Writing, Linguistics
Description: In the B.A. in English program, you will gain a broad liberal arts education and build critical thinking and writing skills that are highly valued in careers in education, publishing, communications, politics and law.  As an English major, you will undergo intensive training in creative and/or professional writing and develop your professional communication skills.  You will examine a variety of literary genres and form a solid understanding of how English language and literature shape and reflect cultures around the world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science
Concentration: Ecological Restoration, Policy Planning and Management, Culture and Communication, Integrated Sciences, Sustainability Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science at the University of Idaho is an interdisciplinary program that brings together faculty and courses from across the university. It provides a framework to address environmental issues by exploring them through various lenses, such as science, policy, society, and restoration, preparing students for diverse careers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Exercise, Sport, and Health Sciences
Concentration: Fitness, Health, and Human Performance, Pre-Physical Therapy & Allied Health, Pre-Athletic Training, Physical Education Teacher Certification
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Exercise, Sport, and Health Sciences program provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the scientific principles behind physical activity, health, and human performance. The curriculum covers topics such as exercise physiology, biomechanics, nutrition, and the psychosocial aspects of health, preparing graduates for various careers in fitness, wellness, and healthcare settings. The program integrates classroom learning with hands-on laboratory experiences and internship opportunities to apply skills in real-world environments.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Finance
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Finance at the University of Idaho equips students with the skills to understand and analyze markets, evaluate complex financials for firms, and manage clients' exposure to risk. The program emphasizes developing both business and personal financial strategies that are ethical and effective. Students gain hands-on experience through programs like the on-campus student trading room, where they invest real money and manage funded portfolios.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Fire, Forest and Rangeland Management
Concentration: Wildland Fire, Land and Livestock, Restoration Ecology
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Fire Ecology and Management provides an understanding of fire's holistic role in the environment and helps develop the skills to solve complex problems in natural resources management. As the first major of its kind in the nation, the program emphasizes direct, hands-on learning, preparing graduates to apply their knowledge to issues like air and water quality and the loss of life and property from wildland fires. Students learn techniques for measuring and modeling fire effects, mapping fires, and conducting prescribed burns.
ProgramCategory: Fire Protection##Forestry##Rangeland Resource Science##Environmental Management##Wildlife Management##Water Resource Management

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Description: As a history major at the University of Idaho, you will explore the entire sweep of the human experience, spanning centuries, continents, and cultures. The program helps you develop a rich historical perspective and strong skills in research, writing, problem-solving, and critical thinking. This equips you for a variety of careers in fields such as business, education, law, and communications.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Interior Architecture and Design
Description: The Bachelor of Interior Architecture and Design (B.I.A.D.) program focuses on solving problems to enhance how people live, work, and play by combining materials, lighting, colors, and furnishings.  This CIDA-accredited professional degree provides intensive design studio experience, preparing students for real-world client projects.  The curriculum is designed to create spaces that are both functional and aesthetically pleasing.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Studies
Concentration: international relations, global resources and development, international economics and business
Description: In this program, you will learn about international political, economic and social issues, become proficient in a foreign language and develop expertise in a region of the globe that interests you. Students become immersed in an international culture through a study abroad experience. This program equips you with the knowledge and skills to thrive in international careers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism
Description: As a journalism major, you will learn how to gather and share newsworthy information across multiple forms of media, including print, broadcast and digital media. You will develop exceptional research and writing skills, sharp news judgment, and gain the global awareness you need for a career in journalism. Students in this program build practical media experiences with opportunities to contribute to the student newspaper, student magazine and university radio station.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Journalism
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Journalism at the University of Idaho equips students to gather and disseminate newsworthy information across various media platforms, including print, broadcast, and digital. The curriculum focuses on developing strong research and writing skills, sharp news judgment, and the global awareness necessary for a successful journalism career. Students gain practical experience through contributions to student-run media like the newspaper, magazine, and radio station.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marketing
Concentration: General Marketing, Sales Management, Entrepreneurship, PGA Golf Management
Description: As a marketing major at the University of Idaho, students study how packaging, advertising, branding, and social media influence consumer behaviors. The curriculum focuses on learning business by doing business, where students explore market research tools and learn to use the marketing mix (product, price, place, promotion) to create effective marketing strategies. The program prepares students for a wide range of marketing careers by developing their ability to think critically and strategically.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Concentration: Aerospace, Computer-aided engineering, Mechanical design and manufacturing, Material behavior and performance, Robotics engineering, Thermal energy system design and analysis
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering program at the University of Idaho teaches students to apply math, science, and engineering principles to design, analyze, and optimize machines, energy systems, and processes. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on learning through a nationally recognized interdisciplinary capstone program, team-based design projects, and extensive internship opportunities. The program prepares graduates for careers in a wide range of industries, including aerospace, automotive, energy, manufacturing, and robotics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music
Concentration: Applied Music
Description: Offered through the nationally accredited Lionel Hampton School of Music, the Bachelor of Arts in Music is an interdisciplinary major for students pursuing careers in music and another field. This broad liberal arts degree allows students to refine their musical talent through intensive training in theory, history, and performance while building a strong foundation in the humanities and sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music
Concentration: Music Performance, Music Education, Music Composition
Description: As a performance major, you will join a community of dedicated artists and grow as a musician through focused study, individualized instruction, ensemble participation, and masterclasses with distinguished faculty. Courses in music theory, history, and performance practice will deepen your understanding of the art form and prepare you for the professional world. An audition is required for admission into all Bachelor of Music programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy
Concentration: Philosophy of Alcohol, Topics in Social Philosophy, Mind and Madness, Philosophy in Film, Buddhism, Feminism and Philosophy
Description: As a philosophy major, you will explore fundamental questions surrounding the nature of human life, reality, and society. You will study the writings of famous philosophers, like Plato and Aristotle, and learn how to think critically and analytically about complex global issues related to politics, justice, professional ethics, the environment, and science.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Concentration: American Political Institutions & Behavior, Public Administration and Public Policy, International and Comparative Politics
Description: In the Bachelor of Arts in Political Science program at the University of Idaho, students examine the science behind politics and the factors that help governments work.  Majors explore contemporary political issues such as health care and education, and study the history of governments worldwide, learning about topics like globalization, American presidencies, and political conflict.  The program emphasizes a traditional liberal arts education, which includes a foreign language requirement.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Political Science
Concentration: American Political Institutions & Behavior, Public Administration and Public Policy, International and Comparative Politics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Political Science at the University of Idaho provides a comprehensive understanding of government systems, political behavior, and policy formulation at both domestic and international levels.  Students explore modern-day political issues, study the history of governments, and learn about topics like globalization and political conflict.  The program emphasizes developing critical thinking, research, and analytical skills to prepare students for careers in public policy, law, and advocacy.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Special Interest, Cultural and Diversity

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at the University of Idaho allows students to explore the complexities of the human mind and behavior. The program, available on-campus or online, covers diverse topics such as mental health, human interaction, workplace dynamics, addiction, and consumer behavior. It aims to provide insights into decision-making processes and build skills for careers in counseling, social work, and human resources.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
Description: Explore the science behind the human mind with a Bachelor of Science in psychology from the University of Idaho, available on campus or fully online. In this program, you'll study topics like mental health, relationships, addiction, workplace behavior, and consumer decision-making. You'll also have the opportunity to participate in research studies, building practical skills for careers in counseling, social work, human resources, and more.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in sociology at the University of Idaho provides the tools to understand how societies work, people connect, and change occurs. Students will study core sociological ideas, theories, and research methods while exploring topics like environmental sociology, political movements, social inequality, and community change. This degree builds practical skills in critical thinking, data analysis, and understanding complex issues from multiple perspectives for careers in fields like education, public policy, social services, and law.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sociology
Concentration: Inequalities and Social Action
Description: The Bachelor of Science in sociology at the University of Idaho provides you with the tools to explore how communities work, how people connect, and what drives change. Through the study of pressing social challenges like inequality, climate change, and political conflict, you'll gain new perspectives on the complexities of the modern world. The program helps you develop skills in critical thinking, data analysis, and understanding complex social issues from a scientific perspective.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Soil and Water Systems
Concentration: Environmental Soil Science, Water Science and Management, Agricultural Systems Management
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Soil and Water Systems addresses resource issues related to soil, water quality and quantity, and sustainable food, energy, and agricultural systems.  The program combines expertise in soil science, hydrology, irrigation, precision agriculture, and waste management to study complex ecological processes in both natural and managed environments.
ProgramCategory: Agriculture##Agriculture Plant Sciences##Environmental Science##Water Resource Management##Sustainable Manufacturing

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Theatre Arts program provides students with a comprehensive understanding of theatre, covering performance, scenic, costume, and lighting design, play analysis, theatre technology, directing, and playwriting. Students learn to create live theatre individually and as part of a collaborative production team. The curriculum offers hands-on experience in all aspects of theatre, from performance and design to management and production.
ProgramCategory: Theater Arts##Performing Arts##Visual and Performing Arts

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre Arts
Concentration: performance (acting), DTM (design, theatre technology, and management)
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre Arts is a rigorous training program for students aiming for a career in professional theatre.  The program provides hands-on training in creating, performing, and producing live theatre, both individually and as part of a team.  Students engage in all aspects of theatrical works, including performance, design, management, and production.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Wildlife Sciences
Concentration: Wildlife Science and Management, Conservation Law Enforcement, Human-Wildlife Interactions
Description: The Bachelor of Science in wildlife sciences at the University of Idaho prepares students to conserve wildlife and manage natural habitats through science-based decision making and in-the-field experiences. This program focuses on the ecology, behavior, and management of wildlife species and the habitats they depend on. Students learn to identify regional species and ecosystems, understand population dynamics, and apply their knowledge through fieldwork and lab research.
